chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he held the leader, the driver, and the rider liable, and he said:
Whatever the foot causes is upon the driver, and whatever the hand causes is upon the rider and the leader.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبِ: the rider mounted on the animal
key_terms.الرِّجْلُ: the foot or hind leg of the animal, indicating damage caused from behind
key_terms.السَّائِقِ: the one driving the animal from behind
key_terms.الْقَائِدِ: the one leading the animal from the front
key_terms.الْيَدُ: the hand, here referring to the forepart or front action of the animal
key_terms.ضَمَّنَ: he imposed liability or responsibility for compensation

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, who is liable for damage caused by an animal being ridden, driven, or led?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a ruling of liability for harm caused by an animal or mount under human control. It assigns responsibility according to the position of control: what is caused by the feet is borne by the driver, while what is caused by the forepart is borne by the rider and the one leading it.
